cards.explanation: The answer is the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza. The angel says, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.” (Acts 8:26) That's a road name and a direction, and the next verse says Philip started out. I once followed a recipe with less detail than that, and the cookies still came out better than my first attempts.

The answer is to worship. The text says he “…had gone to Jerusalem to worship…” (Acts 8:27) That's a long trip for a man with a big job, and he made it anyway. Friends, I think that tells you where his heart was.

The answer is False. The Spirit says, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.” (Acts 8:29) Not away, but BY it. Philip got a clear order and ran straight toward it, which is more than I can say for me with a dirty mixing bowl.

The answer is, “Do you understand what you are reading?” (Acts 8:30) Philip doesn't open with a speech or a sales pitch. He opens with a question, which I think is a pretty kind way to walk up to a stranger.

The answer is False. The official answers, “How can I… unless someone guides me?” (Acts 8:31) A powerful official admits he needs a guide and invites Philip to come up and sit with him. That's honest, friends, and I wish I'd had that kind of honesty back when my stamps came out blurry.

The answer is whether the prophet means himself or someone else. The official asks, “Tell me… who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?” (Acts 8:34) It's a sharp question, and he asks it right out loud. I think a man who asks that is paying close attention.

The answer is Jesus. Philip “…began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.” (Acts 8:35) He started right where the man was reading, and I love that. No detours, friends, just the page in front of them.

The answer is True. The official says, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?” (Acts 8:36) They're traveling along the road when they come to some water, and he speaks right up. I think that man was READY.
The answer is rejoicing. The official “…went on his way rejoicing.” (Acts 8:39) The eunuch saw Philip no more, but he went on his way full of joy. That's a happy ending, friends.

The answer is that Philip preaches the gospel in every town all the way to Caesarea. He “…appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.” (Acts 8:40) The Spirit carried him off, and he just kept right on working. I'd have needed a nap and a cookie, maybe four.
